reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point in Italy tagged as a data center is probably a mistagged professional-services office, not a real facility.

The name carries two signals. "Studio" is the ordinary Italian word for a professional practice, and "Srl" is the standard suffix for a limited-liability company. Neither suggests hosting, colocation, or any commercial computing business. The tag says telecom=data_center, but the name reads as a small office that runs its own IT.

This matters for AI infrastructure because the map is an input to how data-center capacity gets counted. A point like this contributes zero megawatts and no operator, so it adds a location without adding load. If such entries accumulate, any tally built from open mapping data will overstate the number of facilities and understate how concentrated real capacity is.

What the data does not establish is what Studio Delta Srl actually does. The research note records that search quota ran out before the firm's line of business could be confirmed, so the mistag reading rests on naming convention alone. The record also gives no power figure, no operator, and no website, which means it cannot be used to argue anything about Italian data-center capacity in either direction.
